title: Copilot Studio: agent node runs an AI agent as a workflow step
summary: The briefing passes: its roadmap facts, billing qualifications and documented controls are supported. The credit-allocation API note should also name the allocation quantity property, which its example already contains.

claims.claim: An agent node hands a workflow step to an AI agent that can reason, call tools and read knowledge before returning a result.
claims.quote: The agent node lets a flow hand a step over to an AI agent that can reason, call tools, and pull from knowledge sources before returning a result.

claims.claim: The environment tenant-draw setting is at Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits > environment > Capacity overages > Draw from the available capacity in my tenant.
claims.quote:
In the navigation pane, select **Licensing**.
Under **Products**, select **Copilot Studio**.
Select **Manage Copilot Credits**.
Select the environment.
Enter the number of Copilot Credits to allocate.
Under **Capacity overages**, clear **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**.

claims.claim: PUT https://api.powerplatform.com/licensing/allocationsV2?api-version=2024-10-01 sets the environment allocation and TenantPool enforcement rule.
claims.fix: Keep the call. Add this sentence to controls[0].note and its rendered counterpart: 'allocatedEntitlements[].allocation.quantity sets the number of credits allocated to the environment.' The property is documented at https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations and already appears in the prose example.

claims.claim: Power Platform admin center > Licensing > Copilot Studio provides the Agent flow actions used by each workflow.

claims.quote: **New agent for this workflow**: Build an inline agent scoped to this workflow. The agent's instructions, tools, knowledge, and output shape are configured in the node itself and travel with the workflow.

claims.claim: An inline agent cannot be reused outside its workflow.
claims.quote:
Can the inline agent be reused outside this workflow?
